action: Kept English reviews only; simple random sample of 2% (seed 42) -> 192,543 rows
reason: 8 GB does not fit in memory; one language = one consistent vocabulary; random sampling keeps class and game proportions (verified)

action: Converted booleans to 0/1, numbers/timestamps to numeric, kept Steam IDs as text; dropped 'Unnamed: 0' (exported row index) and 'language' (constant after filtering)
reason: Correct types are needed for statistics and models; a constant or row-number column carries no information

action: Removed exact copies, repeated review_id and repeated (author, game) pairs: 22 rows
reason: Duplicates over-weight some reviews and can end up in both train and test (optimistic evaluation)

action: 77 impossible values set to NaN or repaired by domain rules
reason: Overflow markers and impossible dates are errors, not real observations; they would distort statistics, scaling and models

action: Lower-case, removed URLs and BBCode tags, collapsed spaces -> review_clean; dropped 3,449 reviews that were empty, broken (> 8,000 chars) or had no letters
reason: Formatting and links carry no sentiment; empty/broken texts cannot be represented by TF-IDF

action: Kept identical short texts written by different players ('good game', ...)
reason: They are different real reviews with their own labels; removing them would distort the class distribution of short reviews

action: Dropped 0 rows without target; filled 243 playtime_at_review values from total playtime; app_name NaN -> 'unknown'; other model features: median / most-frequent imputation + missing flag, fitted on train
reason: Row-level rules use only the same row (no leakage); learned imputation is fitted on train only; median is robust to heavy tails

action: IQR analysis on raw and log scale; extreme but possible values kept; model features: log1p + clipping to the train 0.1%/99.9% quantiles
reason: Heavy tails are real player behaviour, not errors; log + clipping reduce their influence without throwing away customers

action: log1p for counts/playtime (in pipeline); unix timestamps -> datetime; booleans -> 0/1
reason: log1p removes the strong right skew (see table); datetimes are needed for time-based EDA

action: Model input = text + 3 numeric + 3 boolean + game; votes, comments, later playtime and edit dates are EDA-only
reason: These values appear after the review is published; using them would let the model see the future
Same class ratio in every part; test set is reserved for the single final evaluation

action: One-Hot for app_name (rare games -> 'infrequent'); StandardScaler for log-transformed numeric features; everything fitted on train only
reason: Games are nominal (no order); distance/regularisation-based models need comparable scales; fitting on train only prevents leakage
